title: QuRe: Query-Relevant Retrieval through Hard Negative Sampling in Composed Image Retrieval
summary: Major failure of the pinned core selector despite feasible separated endpoints. Reversed pseudocode inequality and two table averages remain Minor. Historical effects and broad human-alignment interpretation remain Needs Evidence.
limitations: No author-code execution or empirical reproduction.
HP-FashionIQ annotation payload, images, checkpoints and per-query scores not acquired.
Only selected source files/ranges inspected; separate supplement availability unresolved.

claim.location: PDF page 11 Algorithm 1 line 6 versus page 4 Equation (7)
claim.text: The hard negative region obeys target score less than candidate score.

assumptions: Scores [10,9,8,4,3,0], target score 10; use the intended two below-target drops.
problems.check: Construct Equation (7) region, then apply displayed Algorithm 1 inequality.
problems.result: Intended candidate scores [4,3] become an empty set.
counterevidence: Equation (7), prose and inspected release all support selecting below target.
problems.impact: Pseudocode inconsistency, not demonstrated historical training reversal.
problems.severity_rationale: Minor: the inequality contradicts Equation (7), surrounding prose and the implemented below-target selection.

acceptance_check.scope: Correct pseudocode direction; no historical objective reversal inferred.

claim.location: PDF page 4 Equations (5)-(7); data/fashionIQ.py and data/cirr.py rerank_score; fashionIQ.py231-248; train_qure.py37-40; configs/fashionIQ/train.json24-27
claim.text: Two valid below-target drop endpoints can be selected for each query.

assumptions: Target can rank last; no guarantee excludes this.
Active reranking, threshold1; target .95 and tail [.9,.8,.6,.3,-.1].
Distinct unit-vector-realizable scores with enough candidates and a feasible separated pair.
problems.check: Retain empty/short-tail checks; exact rational sufficient-tail construction yields sorted drop indices[3,2,1,0], whose adjacent pairs all fail separation>1 despite feasible indices0 and3.
problems.result: Core selector uses unassigned endpoints on a first query, or may retain prior-query endpoints, even when a valid separated pair exists. Arbitrarily long monotone-increment tails give the same search failure.
counterevidence: Warm-up may change score distributions; occurrence in historical experiments is unmeasured.
The pairwise loss identity is valid.
The printed region-selection idea can be used with a complete search/fallback; this implementation does not guarantee it.
problems.impact: Major deterministic failure of the pinned core hard-negative selection update on admissible inputs. No claim historical runs failed or benchmark scores changed.
problems.correction: Use a complete endpoint search or explicit fallback; reset per-query endpoints; define short-tail/tie policies; establish historical revision and incidence.
problems.core_dependency: Query-specific hard-negative selection is the central routine directly called by training when reranking is enabled.
problems.severity_rationale: Major: admissible sufficient-tail construction leaves endpoints unassigned despite a feasible separated pair; larger corpus size does not guarantee completeness.

acceptance_check.scope: Pinned-release deterministic control-flow finding; warm-up, occurrence and historical effects remain unknown. No author function executed.

claim.location: PDF page 6 Table 3 final column, CosMo and MGUR rows
claim.text: Reported average equals the average of R@5 and subset R@1.

assumptions: Displayed component entries are used as printed.
counterevidence: QuRe average 80.52 is correct and its ordering over these rows survives.
problems.correction: Reconcile component and aggregate values with source runs.
problems.severity_rationale: Minor: CosMo and MGUR means contradict their printed components, while QuRe's 80.52 and relative ordering survive.

acceptance_check.scope: Reconcile components and means with historical runs; true historical values not inferred.

clarifications.text: Conditional preference rate does not alone determine overall agreement or direct preference for QuRe's own outputs. Request orientation randomization, denominators, both directions, ties, paired uncertainty and direct output comparisons.
clarifications.decisive_boundary: Four-pair example has conditional rates A=1 > B=.75 but accuracies A=.5 < B=.75; swapping set labels changes A rate to 1/3.
clarifications.counterevidence: Exchangeable randomized orientation can equate population conditional rate and accuracy. CIRCO supplies separate multiple-ground-truth evidence.

clarifications.text: Quantify semantic false negatives and reconcile training-target pool, duplicate entries, separation threshold and selection history with the published sampling description.

repair_verification: Independent scalar checks passed; no repaired author code or new experiment.
remaining_work: Specify boundary policy and exact corpus/sampling.
Supply version-bound paired human data and clarify claim scope.
